en.title: Airbus to Deliver IRIS, France's Next-Generation Military Earth Observation Satellites
en.summary: France's defence procurement agency has awarded the IRIS programme to Airbus Defence and Space and Thales Alenia Space, with two next-generation very high-resolution Earth observation satellites replacing the CSO system to secure French military space imagery; the contract is worth more than 1.5 billion euros and runs to the end of the 2030s.
body: The French defence procurement agency (DGA) has awarded the contract for the IRIS programme to lead contractor Airbus Defence and Space and co-contractor Thales Alenia Space (TAS). IRIS represents the next generation of extremely high-resolution Earth observation satellites for the French Armed Forces. The contract covers the detailed conception, manufacture and testing for two satellites, as well as the control and user ground segments, plus in-orbit operations and maintenance. Scheduled to run until the end of the 2030s, the contract represents more than one and a half billion euros for the entire consortium.

The IRIS satellites will replace the CSO (Optical Space Component) satellites of the MUSIS (Multinational Space-based Imaging System) programme to secure France's operational image-origin intelligence (IMINT) capability from space. The programme aims to ensure the continuity of this capability while improving performance, with higher image quality and lower latency to make images available faster, to meet the needs of the armed forces in a rapidly changing strategic environment. The satellites will acquire day-and-night images across the visible and infrared spectrums of any point on the Earth's surface at extremely high resolution, and will also be able to image space objects to support space surveillance and the characterisation of space threats.

Airbus will provide both satellite platforms, a significant share of the first satellite's payload, and be responsible for the ground segment. TAS will develop a next-generation payload for the second satellite, provide critical elements for the first payload, and contribute to the ground segment. "With this contract, Airbus Defence and Space is contributing to France's sovereignty and strategic autonomy," said Alain Fauré, Head of Space Systems at Airbus Defence and Space. "In addition, this programme strengthens the French supply chain in space-based optical imagery." Like the MUSIS programme, which involves eight European partners, the IRIS programme remains fully open to international cooperation, granting allied nations access to the French system.

zh.title: 法國IRIS軍用觀測衛星將在軌飛行接替CSO，空中巴士主導逾15億歐元計畫
zh.summary: 法國國防採購局已將IRIS計畫授予約空中巴士防務與航太與泰雷茲阿萊尼亞航太，由兩顆新一代極高解析度地球觀測衛星接替CSO系統，確保法軍太空影像情報能力；整體合約金額逾15億歐元，執行至2030年代末。
body: 法國國防採購局已將IRIS計畫合約授予主承包商空中巴士防務與航太與共同承包商泰雷茲阿萊尼亞航太。IRIS是法國武裝部隊新一代極高解析度地球觀測衛星，合約涵蓋兩顆衛星的細部設計、製造與測試，以及地面控制與使用者接收段，並包括在軌運行與維護；合約預定執行至2030年代末，整個聯盟的合約金額逾15億歐元。
IRIS衛星將接替多國太空影像系統計畫下的CSO光學衛星，確保法國自太空取得影像情報的能力不中斷，同時提升效能：影像品質更高、取得影像的延遲更低，以因應武裝部隊在快速變化的戰略環境中的需求。兩顆衛星將在軌飛行，提供全天候可見光與紅外線影像，覆蓋地球表面任何一點，並能對太空物體成像，以支援太空監視與太空威脅特徵分析。
空中巴士將提供兩具衛星平台、首顆衛星酬載的相當部分，並負責地面段；泰雷茲阿萊尼亞航太將為第二顆衛星開發新一代酬載、提供首顆酬載的關鍵元件，並參與地面段。空中巴士防務與航太太空系統負責人Alain Fauré表示，這項合約有助於法國的主權與戰略自主，也強化法國太空光學影像供應鏈。與已有8個歐洲夥伴參與的多國太空影像系統計畫相同，IRIS計畫也完全開放國際合作，讓盟國得以使用法國的系統。
